lesson.title: Introduction to Flutter
lesson.description: A beginner-friendly introduction to Flutter framework

content.title: What is Flutter?
content.description: Flutter is an open-source UI software development kit created by Google. It's used to develop applications for Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, and the web from a single codebase.

content.definition: The basic building blocks of Flutter apps. Everything in Flutter is a widget, including structural elements, stylistic elements, and even layout properties.
content.example: Text('Hello, World!') is a widget that displays a text string.

content.question: What programming language is Flutter primarily built with?
content.explanation: Flutter uses Dart as its primary programming language, which was chosen for its ability to compile to native code and its support for hot reload.

content.title: Hot Reload
content.description: One of Flutter's most popular features is hot reload, which allows you to see the results of your changes almost instantly without restarting your app or losing its state.

content.question: Which widget is used to create a scrollable list of widgets?
content.explanation: The ListView widget is used to create a scrollable list of widgets arranged linearly.
